blind_target.title: Psychological Examining in the United States Army.
blind_target.evidence_quote: To further test the viability of the one-factor model, we performed confirmatory factor analysis on two correlation matrices of Army Beta data for World War I draftees ([15], pp. 390, 634).
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote: To further test the viability of the one-factor model, we performed confirmatory factor analysis on two correlation matrices of Army Beta data for World War I draftees ([15], pp. 390, 634).
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote: Thus, even in two samples of World War I draftees—groups that would be much more likely to have a separate factor for recognition of written numbers than a modern sample of college students—a one-factor model fit the data just as well as a two-factor model. Again, parsimony dictates that researchers should favor a one-factor model of intelligence from the historic Army Beta data.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: A secondary reproduction reanalyses two original correlation matrices using alternative factor models to test the substantive validity finding. Recovering original reported coefficients was outside this analysis; the original general-ability interpretation survives the tested alternative. Both matrices belong to one original volume.
